title.rendered: The Invitation to Rest: Come to Me, All Who Labour | Living from Rest, Day 1

excerpt.rendered: Matthew 11:28 is the most tender invitation Jesus ever gave. Day 1 of a new series on how a believer learns to live from the rest Jesus bought.

content.rendered:
Jesus did not whisper this. He said it out loud, to a crowd of tired people, in the hearing of history. The invitation still stands this morning: come, and I will give you rest.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, November 1, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 1

Today’s Scripture

“Come to Me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”
Matthew 11:28-30 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Over the next fourteen mornings we will walk, slowly, through a theme the Bible will not let us escape: the Christian life is lived from rest, not towards it. Rest is not the finish line we labour to reach. It is the gift we were brought into the moment we came to Jesus. Everything we build, do and face from here on, we build and do and face from a settled place in Him.

Matthew 11:28, in the NKJV, says, “Come to Me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” The AMPC says, “Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy-laden and overburdened, and I will cause you to rest. [I will ease and relieve and refresh your souls.]” The TPT says, “Are you weary, carrying a heavy burden? Then come to me. I will refresh your life, for I am your oasis.”

Notice what is not in the invitation. Jesus does not say, “Come to Me after you have fixed yourselves.” He does not say, “Come to Me when you have proven you can carry the weight.” He addresses the people who are already labouring and already heavy laden. Those are not two groups. They are one group of people who are both working hard and crushed under what they are working at. Jesus looks across that crowd, which includes every one of us at some point, and He says, come.

Rest in Scripture is not the absence of work. It is the presence of a Person. Hebrews 4 will tell us there is a rest remaining for the people of God, and that rest is entered by faith. John 15 will tell us we are to abide in the vine. Isaiah 30 will tell us that in returning and rest shall we be saved, in quietness and confidence shall be our strength. The same note sounds across the whole Bible. The Christian life is not performed; it is received, lived out of a place of being with Him. That is why the first day of this series is simply an invitation. Before we talk about anything else, you have to come.

So this morning, from Lagos to London, Manila to Nairobi, São Paulo and far beyond, before any plan or project or problem, come. Lay down the load. Not for long, if you cannot. Lay it down for one breath. Receive what He said He would give. “I will give you rest.”

What Rest Actually Means

Rest is a Person before it is a feeling. You are not chasing a mood. You are coming to Jesus.

Rest is received, not earned. You do not qualify for it; you accept it.

Rest is where you work from. You will still work this week. You will just work from a different seat.

Declaration

I come to Jesus this morning. I bring the labour, the load, the heavy things I have been carrying alone. I lay them at His feet. I receive the rest He promised, not because I have earned it, but because He has given it. I am in Christ, and in Christ I am at rest. From that rest I will live, work, speak and love today. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
